svg.title: Cloud system design: migrate, design, and plan for disaster
svg.desc: Top: migration strategies arranged from least to most change. Retire means shutting down what is no longer needed. Retain means keeping it on-premises for now. Rehost, or lift and shift, moves a server as-is to a cloud VM. Replatform makes small changes, such as moving a database to a managed service. Repurchase replaces the app with a SaaS product. Refactor rebuilds the app as cloud-native. More change brings more cloud benefit. Middle left: a monolith is one large application that must scale as a whole, while a cloud-native design splits it into small microservices behind an API gateway that scale independently. Middle right: disaster recovery sites. A hot site is fully running and recovers in minutes at the highest cost; a warm site is partly ready and recovers in hours; a cold site is space and power only, recovers in days, and costs least. Bottom: a timeline around a disaster. The recovery point objective, RPO, is how much data you can afford to lose, measured back to the last backup. The recovery time objective, RTO, is how long the service can be down, measured forward to when service is restored.
svg.text: scales and fails as a whole
microservices scale on their own; here the cart scales out
faster recovery costs more; match the site to the RTO
Smaller RPO means backing up more often. Smaller RTO means a faster, usually costlier, recovery site.
